name: No-Boil Chicken Pasta Casserole with Artichokes and Peas

ingredients.buy: 12 oz (2 1/3 of the 5.2 oz packages), crumbled
1 lb 4 oz drained (about 2 1/3 cans), roughly chopped
2 1/3 tsp finely grated (zest of the same lemons)

writer_notes: Locked view is the source recipe scaled a consistent 2 1/3x to 14 servings (penne 12oz->28oz, chicken 1.5lb->3.5lb, broth 2.5c->5.75c, etc.). All 13 lines scale at the same 2.333 multiplier.

CAPACITY FLAG: source is written for one 9x13 at original size; 2.33x will not fit a single 9x13. Prose and schema steps direct two 9x13 dishes or one large roasting pan. Confirm intended vessel before publish.
All 13 bought ingredients are used by a step; no orphans and no step invents an unbought ingredient.

Cost carried only as the ${{cost_ps}} token because no cost_lines were provided in this dispatch; shop_smart makes no per-ounce or dollar claims, only package-count arithmetic drawn from the locked buy strings.
Macros written as {{cal}}/{{protein}} tokens in prose; head.description uses literal 603 cal and 54.8g protein, which match the locked view exactly.
Garnish parsley scales to 7 tbsp, large but garnish-only and consistent with the 2.33x factor.

prose.intro_html:
Here is the thing about weeknight cooking after a long day. The pasta pot, the strainer, the splatter, the second pan for the sauce. This casserole skips every bit of it. You dump uncooked penne straight into the dish, pour a blended cottage cheese and Boursin sauce over the top, and let the oven do the boiling for you.

And do not let the word casserole trick you into thinking light. At {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein per serving, this is a real dinner that keeps you full until morning. Chicken breast, pasta, artichokes, and peas all in one dish, portioned into fourteen containers that reheat like a dream.
prose.shop_smart:
Read the shopping list before you leave the house, because a couple of these round up in ways that catch you at the register. The sauce leans on two dairy players. You need 12 ounces of Boursin, and it sells in 5.2 ounce boxes, so plan on three of them with a little left over. Cottage cheese is easier, one large tub in the 2 pound range covers the 2 pound 5 ounce call.

Penne runs 1 pound 12 ounces dry, which is just shy of two standard one pound boxes, so grab two and you are set with a handful of pasta to spare. Canned artichoke hearts come in roughly 14 ounce cans, and you want about three of them to land at 1 pound 4 ounces drained. Frozen peas are the move here for a batch this size, one bag covers the 2 1/3 cups without any trimming or shelling. Grate the parmesan off a wedge yourself if you can, it melts better than the pre-shredded stuff. Buy two lemons for both the juice and the zest, and pick up a small bunch of parsley for the finish.
prose.make_it:
Start by getting the oven hot at 400 degrees. Grease your baking dish and set it aside. A batch this size is more than one 9x13 will hold, so split it across two 9x13 dishes or reach for one large roasting pan. Either way the method is identical.

Make the sauce in a blender or food processor. Combine the cottage cheese, crumbled Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt. Blend until completely smooth, then pour in the chicken broth and blend again until it is silky. It will look very thin, and that is exactly what you want. The pasta is going to drink it up in the oven.

Now dump and assemble. Lay the uncooked penne across the bottom, then scatter the cubed chicken breast, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts over the top. Pour the blended sauce over everything, and make sure every noodle is submerged. Anything sticking out will dry hard.

Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Pull it out, take off the foil, and give it a good stir. The pasta should still be a touch undercooked at this point. Top with the grated parmesan and slide it back in for another 5 to 10 minutes, bumping the heat up if you want a golden top. If the pasta is already al dente, just add the parmesan and let it rest.

Rest for at least 10 minutes before you touch it. Finish with chopped parsley or basil and serve.
prose.portion_html:
This recipe splits into fourteen containers, and the honest way to make them even is to weigh, not eyeball. Set an empty container on the kitchen scale and zero it out. Weigh the full baked dish, subtract the pan, divide what is left by fourteen, and that number is your target grams per container. Fill each one to that weight and you will not shortchange container fourteen to overfill container one.

Every portion lands at {{protein}} grams of protein and {{cal}} calories, which is a genuine dinner and not a snack. Let the containers cool uncovered for a few minutes before you lid them so the pasta does not steam into mush, then get them in the fridge.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is where the no-boil trick pays you back twice. It saves you a pot to scrub, and it saves you real money, because the whole dish comes in at about ${{cost_ps}} per serving. That is fourteen high-protein dinners built mostly from pantry and freezer staples.

Compare that to grabbing a chicken pasta bowl from the counter down the street, where a single lunch costs more than several of these containers combined. Cooking the batch yourself is the cheat code, and the flavor does not suffer one bit for the savings.

head.description: No-boil chicken pasta casserole with artichokes and peas. A dump-and-bake blender-sauce dinner that makes 14 high-protein meal-prep servings at 603 calories and 54.8g protein each.
head.keywords: chicken pasta casserole, no boil pasta bake, dump and bake casserole, high protein meal prep, artichoke chicken pasta, boursin pasta bake, chicken casserole meal prep, budget meal prep dinner
steps: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F and lightly grease your baking dish. For a 14-serving batch, use two 9x13 dishes or one large roasting pan.

In a blender or food processor, combine the cottage cheese, crumbled Boursin, minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, lemon zest, and sea salt. Blend until smooth, add the chicken broth, and blend again until silky and thin.

Spread the uncooked penne across the bottom of the dish. Scatter the cubed chicken breast, peas, and chopped artichoke hearts on top, then pour the sauce over everything until the pasta is fully submerged.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Remove the foil, stir well, and check that the pasta is still slightly undercooked.
Top with the grated parmesan and bake uncovered another 5 to 10 minutes until golden. Rest at least 10 minutes, then garnish with chopped parsley or basil and serve.
